title: Keycloak & On-Prem Ops
summary: Automate Keycloak via its admin REST API, validate OIDC config drift against Harbor, and build a health check script for your on-prem clusters. Directly useful for MD-2454 and the Kinetic-ID setup.

sections.title: Keycloak admin REST API
sections.body:
Keycloak has a full REST API. The admin client authenticates with client credentials or username/password.

```python
import requests
import os

class KeycloakAdmin:
    def __init__(self, base_url, realm, client_id, client_secret):
        self.base = base_url.rstrip("/")
        self.realm = realm
        self.session = requests.Session()
        self.session.headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
        self._token = None
        self._authenticate(client_id, client_secret)

    def _authenticate(self, client_id, client_secret):
        """Get admin access token using client credentials."""
        r = self.session.post(
            f"{self.base}/realms/{self.realm}/protocol/openid-connect/token",
            data={
                "grant_type": "client_credentials",
                "client_id": client_id,
                "client_secret": client_secret,
            },
            headers={"Content-Type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"},
            timeout=(5, 30),
        )
        r.raise_for_status()
        self._token = r.json()["access_token"]
        self.session.headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {self._token}"

    def get(self, path, **params):
        r = self.session.get(
            f"{self.base}/admin/realms/{self.realm}{path}",
            params=params, timeout=(5, 30)
        )
        r.raise_for_status()
        return r.json()

    def post(self, path, body):
        r = self.session.post(
            f"{self.base}/admin/realms/{self.realm}{path}",
            json=body, timeout=(5, 30)
        )
        r.raise_for_status()
        return r

    def put(self, path, body):
        r = self.session.put(
            f"{self.base}/admin/realms/{self.realm}{path}",
            json=body, timeout=(5, 30)
        )
        r.raise_for_status()
        return r

# Usage
kc = KeycloakAdmin(
    base_url=os.environ["KEYCLOAK_URL"],
    realm="master",
    client_id="admin-cli",
    client_secret=os.environ["KEYCLOAK_SECRET"],
)

# List clients
clients = kc.get("/clients")
for c in clients:
    print(f"  {c['clientId']:<30} protocol={c.get('protocol','?')} enabled={c['enabled']}")

# List users
users = kc.get("/users", max=100)
for u in users:
    print(f"  {u['username']:<30} email={u.get('email', '?')}")

# Get client by ID
harbor_client = kc.get("/clients", clientId="harbor")
```

sections.title: Detecting OIDC config drift between Keycloak and Harbor
sections.body:
Your MD-2454 work involves wiring Keycloak OIDC into Harbor. This script validates the config is correct on both sides.

```python
import requests
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Optional

@dataclass
class OIDCConfig:
    provider_url:   str
    client_id:      str
    scope:          str
    admin_group:    Optional[str] = None
    auto_onboard:   bool = True
    verify_cert:    bool = True


def get_harbor_oidc_config(harbor_url, auth) -> OIDCConfig:
    """Read Harbor's OIDC config from the API."""
    r = requests.get(
        f"{harbor_url}/api/v2.0/configurations",
        auth=auth, timeout=(5, 30)
    )
    r.raise_for_status()
    cfg = r.json()
    return OIDCConfig(
        provider_url  = cfg.get("oidc_endpoint", {}).get("value", ""),
        client_id     = cfg.get("oidc_client_id", {}).get("value", ""),
        scope         = cfg.get("oidc_scope", {}).get("value", ""),
        admin_group   = cfg.get("oidc_admin_group", {}).get("value"),
        auto_onboard  = cfg.get("oidc_auto_onboard", {}).get("value", True),
        verify_cert   = cfg.get("oidc_verify_cert", {}).get("value", True),
    )


def get_keycloak_oidc_metadata(keycloak_url, realm) -> dict:
    """Read Keycloak's OIDC discovery endpoint."""
    r = requests.get(
        f"{keycloak_url}/realms/{realm}/.well-known/openid-configuration",
        timeout=(5, 30)
    )
    r.raise_for_status()
    return r.json()


def check_harbor_client_exists(kc: 'KeycloakAdmin', client_id: str) -> bool:
    """Verify the Harbor client exists in Keycloak."""
    clients = kc.get("/clients", clientId=client_id)
    return len(clients) > 0


def validate_oidc_config(
    harbor_url,  harbor_auth,
    keycloak_url, keycloak_realm,
    expected_client_id="harbor",
) -> list[str]:  # returns list of issues
    issues = []

    harbor_cfg  = get_harbor_oidc_config(harbor_url, harbor_auth)
    kc_meta     = get_keycloak_oidc_metadata(keycloak_url, keycloak_realm)

    expected_provider = f"{keycloak_url}/realms/{keycloak_realm}"

    # Check 1: Harbor points to the right Keycloak realm
    if harbor_cfg.provider_url.rstrip("/") != expected_provider.rstrip("/"):
        issues.append(
            f"Provider URL mismatch:\n"
            f"  Harbor has:    {harbor_cfg.provider_url}\n"
            f"  Expected:      {expected_provider}"
        )

    # Check 2: Client ID matches
    if harbor_cfg.client_id != expected_client_id:
        issues.append(f"Client ID mismatch: Harbor={harbor_cfg.client_id}, expected={expected_client_id}")

    # Check 3: Required scopes present
    scopes = set(harbor_cfg.scope.split())
    required = {"openid", "profile", "email"}
    missing = required - scopes
    if missing:
        issues.append(f"Missing OIDC scopes: {missing}")

    return issues


# Run validation
issues = validate_oidc_config(
    harbor_url="https://harbor.example.com",
    harbor_auth=("admin", "harbor_password"),
    keycloak_url="https://keycloak.example.com",
    keycloak_realm="platform",
)

if not issues:
    print("✓ Keycloak/Harbor OIDC config is consistent")
else:
    print("✗ Config drift detected:")
    for issue in issues:
        print(f"  - {issue}")
    sys.exit(1)
```

sections.title: On-prem cluster health check script
sections.body:
For your Kinetic-ID / MicroK8s clusters — a health check that can run from CI or a cron job.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""On-prem cluster health check — for MicroK8s / k3s environments."""

import subprocess
import json
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import List

@dataclass
class HealthResult:
    component: str
    ok: bool
    message: str = ""
    details: dict = field(default_factory=dict)


def check_kubectl_access(context=None) -> HealthResult:
    args = ["kubectl", "cluster-info"]
    if context:
        args += ["--context", context]
    result = subprocess.run(args, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10)
    ok = result.returncode == 0
    return HealthResult(
        component="cluster-access",
        ok=ok,
        message=result.stdout.split("\n")[0] if ok else result.stderr.strip()
    )


def check_nodes(context=None) -> List[HealthResult]:
    args = ["kubectl", "get", "nodes", "-o", "json"]
    if context:
        args += ["--context", context]
    result = subprocess.run(args, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=15)
    if result.returncode != 0:
        return [HealthResult("nodes", False, result.stderr.strip())]

    nodes = json.loads(result.stdout)["items"]
    results = []
    for node in nodes:
        name = node["metadata"]["name"]
        conditions = node["status"].get("conditions", [])
        ready = next((c for c in conditions if c["type"] == "Ready"), None)
        ok = ready and ready["status"] == "True"
        results.append(HealthResult(
            component=f"node/{name}",
            ok=ok,
            message=ready["message"] if ready else "No Ready condition"
        ))
    return results


def check_critical_pods(context=None, namespaces=("kube-system",)) -> List[HealthResult]:
    results = []
    for ns in namespaces:
        args = ["kubectl", "get", "pods", "-n", ns, "-o", "json"]
        if context: args += ["--context", context]
        result = subprocess.run(args, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=15)
        if result.returncode != 0:
            results.append(HealthResult(f"pods/{ns}", False, result.stderr))
            continue
        pods = json.loads(result.stdout)["items"]
        for pod in pods:
            name = pod["metadata"]["name"]
            phase = pod["status"].get("phase", "Unknown")
            restarts = sum(
                cs.get("restartCount", 0)
                for cs in pod["status"].get("containerStatuses", [])
            )
            ok = phase == "Running" and restarts < 5
            if not ok:
                results.append(HealthResult(
                    component=f"pod/{ns}/{name}",
                    ok=False,
                    message=f"phase={phase} restarts={restarts}"
                ))
    return results


def run_health_check(context=None):
    results = []
    results.append(check_kubectl_access(context))
    results.extend(check_nodes(context))
    results.extend(check_critical_pods(context))

    passed = [r for r in results if r.ok]
    failed = [r for r in results if not r.ok]

    print(f"\n=== Cluster Health: {context or 'current'} ===")
    for r in failed:
        print(f"  [✗] {r.component}: {r.message}")
    print(f"\n{len(passed)}/{len(results)} checks passed")
    return len(failed) == 0

if __name__ == "__main__":
    ok = run_health_check()
    sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)
```

sections.title: Exercise: OIDC drift checker + cluster health in one tool
sections.body:
Combine both into `ops_check.py` — a single tool with two subcommands:

```bash
python3 ops_check.py cluster-health
python3 ops_check.py oidc-check --harbor-url https://harbor.example.com
```

Try the cluster health part in the terminal now:

```bash
# Get all pods and flag the bad ones
kubectl get pods -A -o json | jq -r '
  .items[] |
  select(.status.phase != "Running") |
  [.metadata.namespace, .metadata.name, .status.phase] | @tsv
'

# Check node status
kubectl get nodes -o json | jq -r '
  .items[] |
  .metadata.name as $name |
  .status.conditions[] |
  select(.type == "Ready") |
  [$name, .status, .message] | @tsv
'

# Simulate the full health check script
python3 << 'EOF'
import subprocess, json

result = subprocess.run(
    ['kubectl', 'get', 'pods', '-A', '-o', 'json'],
    capture_output=True, text=True
)
pods = json.loads(result.stdout)['items']
problems = [
    f"{p['metadata']['namespace']}/{p['metadata']['name']}: {p['status'].get('phase', '?')}"
    for p in pods
    if p['status'].get('phase') not in ('Running', 'Succeeded')
]
if problems:
    print('Issues found:')
    for p in problems: print(f'  ✗ {p}')
else:
    print('All pods healthy')
EOF
```

This is your capstone — combine everything from weeks 4–11 into one deployable tool.
